knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Line Integral of a Vector-Valued Function Along a Union of Curves

question.:question/problem:
![](images/c0/c0a4f042748ddadd824bed4ee71bca9724d7ca7dcc376a0ccf7c1353d59ec4fc.png)

The path ${C}_{1}$ consists of a line segment from the point $A(-2,2)$ to the point $B(-1,2),$ and the path ${C}_{2}$ consists of a line segment from the point $B(-1,2)$ to the point $D(-1,0).$

Traverse $C=C_1\cup C_2$ in the stated order. Let

$$
\mathbf F(x,y)=(2 x + y)\mathbf i+(2 x)\mathbf j.
$$

Given that

$$
\int_{C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=-1,
$$

evaluate $\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r$.

For $C_2$, use $\mathbf r_2(t)=(-1)\mathbf i+(2 - 2 t)\mathbf j$, with $t$ running from $0$ to $1$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use additivity over the two oriented pieces.

$$
\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=\int_{C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r+\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r
$$

The contribution from $C_1$ is supplied, so calculate $C_2$ only. Choose $x=-1$ and $y=2 - 2 t$, with $t$ running from $0$ to $1$ in that order. The endpoint substitutions give the start and end of the stated piece.

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_2(t)&=(-1)\mathbf i+(2 - 2 t)\mathbf j, \\ \mathbf r_2'(t)&=(0)\mathbf i+(-2)\mathbf j.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the field components:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mathbf r_2(t))&=- 2 t, \\ Q(\mathbf r_2(t))&=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the dot product, keeping both tangent factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf F(\mathbf r_2(t))\cdot\mathbf r_2'(t)&=(- 2 t)(0) \\ &\quad+(-2)(-2) \\ &=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate in the specified direction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=\int_{0}^{1}(4)\,\mathrm dt \\ &=\left[4 t\right]_{0}^{1} \\ &=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Add the supplied contribution:

$$
\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=(-1)+(4)=3.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Line Integral of a Vector-Valued Function Along a Union of Curves

question.:question/problem:
![](images/b4/b4ce481ac8babb7a3e5707f1ef44417b12e73abe4b4c2143c19b45332642c6d2.png)

The path ${C}_{1}$ consists of a line segment  from the point $B(0,8)$ to the point $A(-2,8),$ and the path ${C}_{2}$ consists of a section of the curve $y=-{x}^{3}$ from the point $A(-2,8)$ to the point $O(0,0).$

Traverse $C=C_1\cup C_2$ in the stated order. Let

$$
\mathbf F(x,y)=(x y)\mathbf i+(2 y)\mathbf j.
$$

Given that

$$
\int_{C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=16,
$$

evaluate $\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use additivity over the two oriented pieces.

$$
\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=\int_{C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r+\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r
$$

The contribution from $C_1$ is supplied, so calculate $C_2$ only. Choose $x=t$ and $y=- t^{3}$, with $t$ running from $-2$ to $0$ in that order. The endpoint substitutions give the start and end of the stated piece.

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_2(t)&=(t)\mathbf i+(- t^{3})\mathbf j, \\ \mathbf r_2'(t)&=(1)\mathbf i+(- 3 t^{2})\mathbf j.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the field components:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mathbf r_2(t))&=- t^{4}, \\ Q(\mathbf r_2(t))&=- 2 t^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the dot product, keeping both tangent factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf F(\mathbf r_2(t))\cdot\mathbf r_2'(t)&=(- t^{4})(1) \\ &\quad+(- 2 t^{3})(- 3 t^{2}) \\ &=6 t^{5} - t^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate in the specified direction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=\int_{-2}^{0}(6 t^{5} - t^{4})\,\mathrm dt \\ &=\left[t^{6} - \frac{t^{5}}{5}\right]_{-2}^{0} \\ &=- \frac{352}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Add the supplied contribution:

$$
\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=(16)+\left(- \frac{352}{5}\right)=- \frac{272}{5}.
$$
